_what: A COACHING SEASON IS HELD IN ONE SHAPE. Ruled by Ryan, 2026-09-09. The person index holds a man's stint seasons in two dicts: `seasons` and `coaching_seasons`. A stint claim belongs to `coaching_seasons` if and only if its PREDICATE is one of the staff predicates below. Nothing decides it by league token, by store name, or by how the man entered the archive.

_the_defect_this_replaces._measured_2026_09_09: The index held coaching seasons in THREE non-overlapping shapes: 7,201 keys in `seasons` under a `COACHES` league token (from coaches, coaches-nfl, assistants -- stores whose declared token is COACHES); 17,067 keys in `seasons` under a REAL league token (from pfa-coaches, whose subjects name NFL-1979); and 12,656 in `coaching_seasons` (written by apply_promotions for men promoted from a coaching lead). Zero keys appeared in both dicts.
_the_defect_this_replaces._why_it_happened: The split was by PROVENANCE, not by meaning. A man who entered the archive as a player and later gained PFA coaching claims got them in `seasons`; a man who existed only as a coach and was promoted from a lead got them in `coaching_seasons`. The same fact landed in a different dict depending on how the man arrived.
_the_defect_this_replaces._what_it_cost: Jack Pardee's `seasons` held `CFL|1995|BIR` -- a coaching claim -- in the dict 53 files read as playing seasons, and his `coaching_seasons` was empty. His served bio said he 'played thirty-two seasons' and 'played for seven clubs', four of which he only coached. 1,758 people were affected across 17,067 seasons.

staff_predicates._what: The predicates that make a stint a COACHING OR STAFF season rather than a playing one. Read on the predicate, never on the league: `pfa.coaching_season` is a coaching season whatever league it names. This list is the archive's, not the service's: src/build_person_index.py and service/classification.py both read it here, so there is one implementation.

not_staff_though_it_appears_in_those_sto.shared_or_split_season: A QUALIFIER on a head-coaching claim, not a staff claim in itself: 469 claims, all in coaches-nfl, all value true. Measured 2026-09-09: 0 (person, club-season) pairs hold it without also holding a declared staff predicate, so it never decides anything alone. It travels with the season it qualifies.

staff_predicates._officials_are_not_here: `pfa.officiating_season` is person_season-scoped and carries no club, because PFA assigns an official to a league and a season and never to a team. There is no stint, so there is no season key and nothing to sort.

_a_player_coach_keeps_both: 330 (person, club-season) pairs hold a playing claim AND a staff claim -- Glenn Dobbs at Saskatchewan, Bill Daddio at Buffalo, and Jack Pardee, who played and coached. The SAME KEY then appears in BOTH dicts, and that is correct and required: the exclusivity is per CLAIM, not per key. A player-coach is never made to choose, and no claim is written twice.
_salaries_stay_in_seasons: The `salaries` store's 26 keys carry no staff predicate -- a court record about a man's PAY at a club is not a coaching season. They stay in `seasons`, which the predicate rule gives for free. `seasons` is therefore 'stints that are not staff', not 'playing stints', and the difference is 26 keys.

_the_league_token_on_a_coaching_key._problem: coaches, coaches-nfl and assistants name no league anywhere -- their season keys read `y1979` -- so build_person_index writes the store's declared token, `COACHES`, in the league position. pfa-coaches names the league on the subject and writes `NFL`. Measured 2026-09-09: 3,281 (person, year, club) triples on 433 men were written TWICE, once under each, so moving both dicts' worth into one place without a rule would hold the same coaching season twice.
_the_league_token_on_a_coaching_key._rule: A `COACHES` key is NOT merged into a real-league key for the same (year, club). Each source keeps its own key, and one coaching club-season is held twice -- `COACHES|1986|BUF` beside `NFL|1986|BUF` -- as TWO ATTESTATIONS, which is what the index has always held when two sources print a club differently; the claims remain the record. Only the year format is normalised (below). Where no source names a league, the token stays `COACHES`, for the reason `SALARIES` exists (declarations/person-index-rebuild.json): the key shape cannot write an empty league.
_the_league_token_on_a_coaching_key._rule_corrected_2026_09_11: CORRECTED (Ryan, 2026-09-11). This declaration used to say a `COACHES` key MERGES into the real-league key. The code does not, deliberately, because merging was TRIED AND BROKE THE CLUB TABLE: build_clubs corroborates a printed club name against a code by finding ONE MAN who holds both for the same league-year -- that is how the Coaching Tree's 'Buffalo Bisons' is known to be the Bills, from 21 person-seasons holding both that string and BUF under COACHES. Folding `COACHES|1986|BUF` into `NFL|1986|BUF` moved one half of every such pair into a different league group, and every wrong-for-season string the Coaching Tree corroborates vanished; gate_clubs K2 caught it. The reasoning is in src/build_person_index.py split_coaching ('THE LEAGUE TOKEN IS LEFT ALONE, and here is why, because it was tried the other way'). A declaration describing behaviour the code abandoned is worse than none. Measured 2026-09-11: 669 people hold one coaching club-season under two keys (4,880 club-seasons) with the merges working -- 3,589 while they were not.
_the_league_token_on_a_coaching_key._year_format: The year in a coaching key is written BARE. `coaches` and friends produced `y1979` because their season key is `y1979` and the builder took the last dash-separated part; pfa-coaches produced `1979`. One shape means one year format, and every consumer already carried `y[1:5] if y.startswith('y') else y` to cope. `seasons` keeps its 26 `y`-prefixed SALARIES keys, which this ruling does not touch.

_gate: src/gate_coaching_season_shape.py. Two properties, both derived from the index and the stores rather than from this file: (1) every (person, season key, predicate) is reachable from EXACTLY ONE of the two dicts -- never both, never neither; (2) a claim's dict follows its PREDICATE, so no staff predicate sits in `seasons` and no non-staff predicate sits in `coaching_seasons`, whatever league token the key carries.

roles._what: WHERE A COACHING ROLE IS READ FROM, and which printed roles are HEAD-COACH roles. Ruled by Ryan, 2026-09-09: a coaching-only bio opens on where he coached, in what roles, across how long. The roles were in the archive all along and nothing read them.
roles._the_defect: src/bio_select.coach_runs took a role only from `role_title` -- the Coaching Tree's predicate -- and took HEAD standing only from `is_head_coach`. PFA's coaching seasons carry neither: they carry `position_as_printed` inside the `pfa.coaching_season` value. Measured 2026-09-09: 1,046 distinct printed positions across 3,356 men, of whom PFA prints 706 as HEAD COACH -- and every one of those 706 was being read as an assistant with no role at all. 997 of the 2,138 coaching-only men then fell into a lead the writer had no branch for and returned 503.
roles._role_predicates_note: `role_title` carries the role directly. The two PFA predicates carry a dict; the role is its `position_as_printed`, held EXACTLY as printed -- 'Offensive Line', 'Assistant Strength and Conditioning', 'HEAD COACH' in PFA's own capitals. Nothing is rewritten or title-cased.

head_coach_positions._what: The printed positions that mean the man WAS THE HEAD COACH that season. The test is on the FIRST slash-separated segment, upper-cased, and only against this list.
head_coach_positions._why_the_first_segment: PFA writes a compound job as 'HEAD COACH/Offensive Coordinator' (14) and also 'Offensive Line/Assistant Head Coach' (4). The first segment is the job; the rest is what else he did. Testing the whole string, or testing for the substring 'head coach', would make an Assistant Head Coach a head coach -- 758 seasons across 30 printed variants -- which is the opposite of what the source says.

_deliberately_excluded.ASSISTANT HEAD COACH: 758 seasons across 30 variants. An assistant head coach is an assistant.
_deliberately_excluded.ASSISTANT TO THE HEAD COACH: and 'ASSISTANT TO HEAD COACH', 'SPECIAL ASSISTANT TO THE HEAD COACH' -- staff to the head coach, not the head coach.
_deliberately_excluded.HEAD STRENGTH AND CONDITIONING: and 'HEAD OFFENSIVE LINE', 'HEAD QUALITY CONTROL' -- head OF something that is not the team.

head_coach_positions._HEAD_OOACH: 1 season. PFA's typo for HEAD COACH, and it is DECLARED here rather than folded by a fuzzy match: the store keeps the string exactly as printed, and this list is the reading that recognises it. An edit-distance rule would also catch things that are not typos.
